n: After the proud “forest” of Assyria is cut down (10:33-34), a new shoot will sprout from the stump of Jesse, King David’s father. D&C 113 explains that the “stem of Jesse” is Christ and the “rod” is a servant in His hands, a descendant of Jesse and Ephraim. Moroni quoted this chapter to Joseph Smith, saying it was about to be fulfilled.

f.g: A shoot or twig sprouting from a stump.

n: The Spirit of the Lord will rest on Him, giving perfect wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, and reverence for God. This describes the Messiah’s divine endowment.

f.w: the spirit of the LORD shall rest upon him

f.g: Reverent awe and devotion toward God.

n: He will delight in revering the Lord. He won’t judge by appearances or rumors, but will see the truth of every heart.

f.g: Literally “his delight” or “his scent” — keen discernment.

f.w: not judge after the sight of his eyes

n: He will judge the poor fairly and defend the humble. His word alone will strike the earth, and His breath will destroy the wicked — fulfilled fully at His Second Coming.
Righteousness and faithfulness will be like the belt He wears — always part of who He is, wrapped around Him.

f.g: Belt — what holds a person ready for action.

n: A famous picture of millennial peace: predators and prey live together, and a little child can lead them. The enmity in nature will end.

f.w: The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb

n: Cows and bears will graze together, their young lying side by side, and lions will eat straw like oxen. Even animal nature will change.

f.w: the lion shall eat straw like the ox

n: A nursing baby will play safely near a cobra’s hole, and a toddler will reach into a viper’s nest unharmed.

f.g: An old word for a poisonous snake, perhaps a viper.

n: Nothing will harm or destroy in God’s holy mountain, because the earth will be filled with knowledge of the Lord as water fills the sea.

f.w: the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the LORD

n: In that day the “root of Jesse” will stand as a banner for the peoples, and the Gentiles will seek Him. D&C 113:5-6 identifies this root as a latter-day descendant of Jesse and Joseph holding priesthood keys; Paul applies the verse to Christ.

The Lord will reach out a second time to gather His scattered people from every land. The first great gathering was the return from Babylon; Latter-day Saints see the second as the latter-day gathering begun with the Restoration.
He will raise a banner to the nations and gather the outcasts of Israel and the scattered of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
The old rivalry between Ephraim (the northern tribes) and Judah will end. They will no longer be jealous of or hostile toward each other — a hope for unity in the gathered house of Israel.
United, Israel will swoop down on its old enemies — the Philistines to the west, and peoples to the east like Edom, Moab, and Ammon. The imagery is of triumph, not literal conquest today.

f.g: Neighbors southeast and east of the Dead Sea, longtime foes of Israel.

n: The Lord will dry up the gulf of the Egyptian sea and divide the great river into seven streams so His people can cross on foot — a new Exodus.

f.w: the tongue of the Egyptian sea
f.g: The Gulf of Suez, an arm of the Red Sea.
With dry sandals — without getting wet.

n: There will be a highway for the returning remnant from Assyria, just as there was when Israel came out of Egypt. God’s past deliverances promise future ones.
